title: Embedding Throughput Topology Optimizer and Queue-aware Autoscaler
creator: Marco Alvarez
description: Problem: Several customers and internal benchmarks show that the embeddings endpoint exhibits poor tail latency and inefficient GPU utilization under mixed-tenant traffic. Current autoscaling reacts to CPU/GPU pressure and simple QPS thresholds, which leads to burst-induced latency spikes, cold-start penalties, and uneven tenant fairness during surge patterns. We need a cohesive design that reduces p99 latency, increases steady-state throughput, and reduces excess reserved capacity costs for Dedicated pools.
acceptance_criteria: 1) p99 end-to-end latency for 16k-query synthetic embedding workload decreases by >=20% in canary traffic vs baseline; 2) steady-state token throughput per GPU increases by >=15% without violating p50 latency SLO; 3) burst-induced tail events are mitigated so that >95% of tenant burst requests are served without dropping to fallback models; 4) autoscaler does not increase long-run baseline capacity (no net >10% committed cost increase).
design_overview: Introduce a Topology Optimizer that assigns tenant routing groups to heterogeneous GPU pools (memory-optimized vs throughput-optimized) based on historical request shape and model variant. Combine with a Queue-aware Autoscaler which uses ingress queue depth, queue growth rate, and effective token backlog rather than raw CPU utilization alone. Key components: 1) Tenant Profiling Service to produce per-tenant request shape signatures (avg tokens, variance, burstiness index); 2) Topology Optimizer scheduler that periodically rebalances tenant assignments to pools to align with pool capabilities; 3) Admission Controller with leaky-bucket smoothing and soft rate fences for tenants; 4) Autoscaler that consumes queue metrics + predicted short-term demand from the forecasting pipeline to provision warm slots; 5) Warm pool management with memory-preserved kernels to avoid cold-start KV-cache penalties.
detailed_plan: Phase 0 - Spike (1 week): build a lightweight simulator that replays anonymized request traces and validates scheduling heuristics. Phase 1 - Prototype (2 weeks): implement Tenant Profiling and a topology decision API; run offline placement tests and small-scale canary in staging. Phase 2 - Queue-aware Autoscaler (3 weeks): implement autoscaler logic, integrate ingress queue metrics (queue_length, queue_growth_rate, token_backlog) and add a short-term forecast hook. Phase 3 - Warm pools and admission controller (2 weeks): implement warm slot lifecycle, kernel preloading, and tenant leaky-bucket smoothing. Phase 4 - Canary rollout (2 weeks): progressive rollout to a subset of tenants behind feature flag with tight monitoring and rollback conditions. Phase 5 - Post-mortem and tuning (1 week).
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Complexity: Adding topology layer increases scheduler complexity and operator burden. We'll guard with a simple opt-in canary and observable runbooks. - Fairness vs Efficiency: Prioritizing throughput may disadvantage small tenants; admission controller will include soft rate fences and explicit fairness quotas. - Forecast accuracy: autoscaler relies on short-term forecasts; poor forecasts can cause oscillation. Mitigation: smoothing windows, cooldowns, and conservative headroom. - Failure modes: Scheduler misplacement could overload a pool; plan includes circuit breaker to revert placements and draining helpers.
monitoring_and_metrics: New and updated metrics: embeddings.queue_length, embeddings.queue_growth_rate, embeddings.token_backlog, topology.assignment_changes, pool.utilization_by_model_variant, autoscaler.scale_events, warm_pool.hits, admission_controller.rejections, tenant.burst_satisfaction. Dashboards: per-tenant latency heatmap, pool-level capacity view, autoscaler decision timeline. Alerts: sustained queue_growth_rate > X for > 30s, unexpected placement flips > 3 in 10m, warm_pool_miss_rate > 5%.
testing_and_validation: - Synthetic load tests across multiple tenant profiles (microburst, steady high qps, variable token size) using the fidelity replay from ENG-913579. - Chaos tests: simulate GPU OOMs, node drains, and spot preemptions to validate graceful fallback. - Regression matrices: compare current autoscaler vs queue-aware autoscaler on cost and latency budgets. - Smoke tests for warm-pool correctness (kernel preloads, KV cache warm-up).
rollout_playbook: 1) Feature flag behind tenant opt-in; 2) Start with internal tenants and low-risk customers; 3) Canary to 3% of production embed QPS for 72 hours; 4) If p99 latency regressions >10% or error rate increase >0.5%, rollback and run incident checklist; 5) Gradually increase to 25% then 100% with weekly tuning windows.
